acquisition method: Mass spectrometry was performed by Q Exactive plus mass spectrometer (Thermo) in a positive mode using a repetitively full MS scan followed by high collision dissociation (HCD) of the ten most dominant ions selected from the first MS scan.
alkylation reagent: modified with 10 mM iodoacetamide in 100 mM ammonium bicarbonate
alkylation concentration: modified with 10 mM iodoacetamide in 100 mM ammonium bicarbonate
cleavage agent: and digested in 10% acetonitrile and 10 mM ammonium bicarbonate with modified trypsin (Promega) at a 1:10 enzyme-to-substrate ratio
enrichment method: Proteins were isolated using anti-Flag M2 beads as described above, and bound proteins were eluted using 2× non-reducing Laemmli sample buffer.
fragmentation method: followed by high collision dissociation (HCD) of the ten most dominant ions
instrument: Mass spectrometry was performed by Q Exactive plus mass spectrometer (Thermo)
labeling: Semi-quantitation was done by calculating the peak area of each peptide based on its extracted ion currents (XICs)
precursor tolerance: with a mass tolerance of 10 ppm for the precursor masses and 0.05 amu for the fragment ions.
fragment tolerance: with a mass tolerance of 10 ppm for the precursor masses and 0.05 amu for the fragment ions.
ptm: Oxidation (M) variable; phosphorylation (S, T, Y) variable; acetylation (K) variable; ubiquitination (K) variable; methylation (K) variable; butyrylation (K) variable; carbamidomethyl on Cys static

Oxidation (M), phosphorylation (S, T, Y), acetylation (K), ubiquitination (K), methylation (K), and butyrylation (K) were accepted as variable modifications, and carbamidomethyl on Cys was accepted as a static modification.
reduction reagent: The sample was reduced with 3 mM DTT (60 °C for 30 min)
reduction concentration: The sample was reduced with 3 mM DTT (60 °C for 30 min)
